hook.situation: You're at a Korean café. You want water, a croissant, and you want to pay by card. You manage to say '물 주세요' — but then you freeze. How do you add 'and the croissant too'? How do you ask if card payment is okay? You need three small but powerful particles: 도 (also), 만 (only), and 로/으로 (by means of).
objectives: Use 도 to add one more item to an order ('and this too, please')
Use 만 to set a limit ('only this, nothing else')
Use 로/으로 to express payment method, transport, or language ('by card', 'in Korean')
hook.whyItMatters: These three particles unlock real transactions. 도, 만, and 로/으로 are used in every café, restaurant, and convenience store interaction in Korea. Without them, every order is a single isolated item — with them, you can build natural, flexible requests that sound like a real customer, not a tourist reading a phrasebook.

grammarNotes.title: 도 vs 만 — also / too vs only
grammarNotes.func: 도 means "also / too" and adds this noun to others; 만 means "only" and shuts out everything else. Both attach straight to a noun and take the place of the topic/subject/object marker (은/는/이/가/을/를) instead of sitting on top of it.

formTable.ex: 저 → 저도, 물 → 물도, 친구 → 친구도
물 → 물만, 밥 → 밥만, 학생 → 학생만
밥을 → 밥도 / 밥만, 책을 → 책도 / 책만

examples.note: 도 takes the place of 는 in 저는 — "me too," on top of the other students.
만 = water and nothing else; super common when you're ordering.
도 adds 친구 to the people already going; it replaces 가 in 친구가.
만 stands in for the object marker 을 in 밥을 — rice and nothing else. (밥만 sounds like [밤만].)

keyPoint.label: 도 vs 만
keyPoint.body: 도 includes (this AND the rest); 만 excludes (this and NOTHING else). Quick test: if "too" fits, use 도; if "just / nothing but" fits, use 만. Either way you drop 은/는/이/가/을/를 first — 저도, never 저는도; 밥만, never 밥을만.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 만 after a 받침 nasalizes the consonant before it: 밥만 sounds like [밤만] (ㅂ → ㅁ before ㅁ).

drill.instruction: Add 도 (also) or 만 (only) to match the English. Drop any 은/는/이/가/을/를 first.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: In English you keep the subject and just bolt on "too," so learners want to hold onto 는/을 and add 도/만 after it. In Korean, 도/만 replace 은/는/이/가/을/를 — strip the old marker off completely, then add 도 or 만.

grammarNotes.title: (으)로 — by / with, and which way
grammarNotes.func: (으)로 marks how you do something — the tool, language, payment method, or transport ("by / with / in") — and also the direction you head ("toward / to"). You'll reach for it constantly when paying and ordering.

formTable.ex: 카드 → 카드로, 버스 → 버스로, 한국어 → 한국어로
손 → 손으로, 젓가락 → 젓가락으로, 현금 → 현금으로

formTable.when: Noun ends in ㄹ 받침 (special case)

formTable.ex: 집 → 집으로, 학교 → 학교로, 이쪽 → 이쪽으로

examples.note: 카드 ends in a vowel → 로. The exact thing you say at the register.
한국어 ends in a vowel → 로; here 로 marks the language you're using.
젓가락 ends in 받침 ㄱ → 으로; marks the tool you use.
집 ends in 받침 ㅂ → 으로; here 로 marks direction, not a means.

keyPoint.label: (으)로 vs 에 (direction)
keyPoint.body: For where you're going, 에 marks the destination you arrive at (집에 가요 = go home), while (으)로 stresses the direction you head (집으로 가요 = head toward home) — at this level either is fine for "go home." Mostly you'll use the "by / with" sense: 카드로, 현금으로, 한국어로. Just watch the ㄹ rule — 지하철로, not 지하철으로.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 으로 after a 받침 pulls the consonant into 으: 손으로 sounds like [소느로], 집으로 like [지브로].

drill.instruction: Add 로 or 으로. Check whether the noun ends in a vowel, a 받침, or ㄹ.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Learners stretch the 받침 → 으로 rule too far. Vowel-final nouns just take 로 (카드로), and ㄹ-final words are a special case that also take plain 로, not 으로 (지하철로, 연필로). Only non-ㄹ 받침 nouns get 으로.

exampleSentence.note: N + 주세요 = the single most useful ordering pattern in Korea
이거 (this) + 얼마예요 — the go-to price question in any market, convenience store, or café
카드 ends in a vowel → 로 (not 으로)
현금 ends in a consonant (ㅁ) → 으로

exampleSentence.en: Is it okay to pay by card?
exampleSentence.note: 결제하다 is the formal word for payment processing; 내다 or 계산하다 are more casual
Direct N 주세요 request — no extra particles needed
주문하다 + 아/어도 돼요? = polite permission request; 받다 (receive) is often said by staff: 주문받겠습니다
메뉴 is a loanword from English; in practice many Korean cafés have menus only on boards, so this is more useful than it sounds
Quantities in ordering use native Korean numbers (하나, 둘, 셋), not Sino-Korean (일, 이, 삼)
좀 softens the request; 좀 주세요 sounds more polite and natural than 주세요 alone
더 = more quantity; often combined with 좀 for a polite, natural request for a refill
카드 돼요? is a spoken shortcut — grammatically incomplete but perfectly natural in shops
이거 is the spoken form, 이것 is written/formal; both work at a café or shop counter
포장 (packing) = takeout in Korean. 포장이요? is how staff ask if you want it to go
추천 없어요? or 추천 메뉴요? are very natural ways to ask a café or restaurant what's good
할인 + 돼요? is the pattern to ask about discounts; 학생 할인, 앱 할인, 포인트 할인 all work the same way
맵게 is the adverbial form (spicily); 안 맵게 해 주세요 = make it in a not-spicy way — practical for dietary restrictions

extendedDialogue.setting: Minjun and his coworker Yuna go to a café. Minjun orders for both of them.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Welcome! What can I get you?
lines.grammarNote: 뭐 드릴까요? — the polite 'what shall I offer you?' form staff use in Korean cafés; 드리다 is the honorific of 주다

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.grammarNote: N 주세요 ordering pattern; 한 잔 = one cup using native Korean number 한 + counter 잔

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.grammarNote: 더 (more/else) here asks if there's anything to add — functions like 도 in a question context

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.grammarNote: 빵 + 도 = adding the bread to the cart (SHOPPING CART rule); 하나 = one (native Korean number)

lines.speaker: 유나
lines.ko: 저는 물만 주세요. 커피는 안 마셔요.
lines.romanization: Jeoneun mulman juseyo. Keopineun an masyeoyo.
lines.en: Just water for me, please. I don't drink coffee.
lines.grammarNote: 물 + 만 = spotlight on water alone (SPOTLIGHT rule); this is 만 as a preference restriction

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Got it. How would you like to pay?
lines.grammarNote: 어떻게 (how) + 하시겠어요? is the polite 'how will you do X?' frame — staff asking the payment method opens the 로/으로 response

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.grammarNote: 카드 + 로 = the CHANNEL SELECTOR (method particle); 카드 ends in vowel 드 → 로, not 으로. 결제해도 돼요? is the polite permission question.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, card is fine. Do you need a receipt?
lines.grammarNote: 카드 됩니다 is the staff-side confirmation; 영수증 주세요 or 영수증도 주세요 is the natural follow-up if you want the receipt

readingText.title: 편의점에서 (At the Convenience Store)
readingText.body: 오늘 편의점에 가요. 과자를 하나 사요. 직원에게 '이거 얼마예요?'라고 물어요. 삼천 원이에요. 현금이 없어요. 그래서 카드로 결제해요. 영수증도 받아요. 음료는 안 사요. 이것만 사요. 다음에는 할인도 확인해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Today I go to a convenience store. I buy one snack. I ask the staff, 'How much is this?' It is 3,000 won. I don't have cash, so I pay by card. I get a receipt too. I don't buy a drink. I buy only this. Next time I check discounts too.

comprehensionQuestions.question: How did the speaker pay, and why?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 카드로 결제해요 — they pay by card because they have no cash (현금이 없어요. 그래서...)

comprehensionQuestions.question: What does the speaker buy, and what do they not buy?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 과자를 하나 사요. 음료는 안 사요 — they buy one snack and do not buy a drink.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Find every 도 and 만 in the text. For each one, explain whether it is adding something or limiting something.
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 영수증도 받아요 — 도 adds the receipt to the list of things that happen (CART: one more item); 이것만 사요 — 만 limits the purchase to only this item (SPOTLIGHT: nothing else); 할인도 확인해요 — 도 adds checking discounts to the plan (CART: another thing to do)

culturalNote.title: 카드 돼요? — Why Korean shops sometimes say no
culturalNote.body: In Korea, '카드 돼요?' (Is card okay?) is a completely natural counter question. In most cafés and convenience stores, card payment is normal, but at street stalls, traditional markets, or very small shops you may still hear '현금만 돼요' (cash only) or see staff point you toward a different payment method. The useful learner move is simple: ask once, then answer with 카드로 할게요 or 현금으로 할게요. Carrying a few small bills is still practical when you explore markets or small food stalls.

inlineExercises.prompt: 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요. 빵___ 하나 주세요. (One Americano, please. Bread too, please.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 도 adds the bread to the order (SHOPPING CART — one more item). If you used 만, the sentence would mean 'only bread, please' — cancelling the Americano you just ordered.

inlineExercises.prompt: 저는 물___ 마셔요. 다른 건 필요 없어요. (I drink only water. I don't need anything else.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 만 is the SPOTLIGHT — it limits the sentence to water and excludes everything else. 도 would mean 'I drink water too (among other things)', which contradicts '다른 건 필요 없어요'.

inlineExercises.prompt: 카드___ 결제할 수 있어요? (Can I pay by card?)
inlineExercises.explanation: 로/으로 marks the method (CHANNEL SELECTOR). 카드에 would mean 'on the card' or 'at the card' as if the card were a location, which makes no sense. The payment flows through the card channel → 카드로.

inlineExercises.prompt: 다음 문장에서 틀린 것을 찾아보세요: '저는도 주문할게요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 도 replaces subject and topic particles — it does not sit after them. 저는 + 도 is a double-particle error; drop 는 and say 저도. The same principle applies to 만: never 이것을만, always 이것만.

inlineExercises.prompt: Translate: 'I'll pay in cash. Receipt too, please.'
inlineExercises.hint: 현금 ends in a consonant → which form? And are you adding the receipt (CART) or limiting to only the receipt (SPOTLIGHT)?
inlineExercises.explanation: -(으)ㄹ게요 shows the speaker's own decision, so 낼게요 fits 'I'll pay.' 도 adds 'also,' making 영수증도 주세요 natural for 'receipt too, please.'

inlineExercises.prompt: The staff asks how you want to pay. You want to ask 'Is it okay if I pay by card?' Which is the most natural?
inlineExercises.explanation: 로/으로 marks the method of payment — the card is the CHANNEL. 카드에 would mean 'at the card' (card as a location — doesn't work). 카드를 would mean 'pay the card' — as if the card itself is the thing being paid, not the payment method.

inlineExercises.prompt: 배고파요? 이거___ 드세요. 다른 건 없어요. (Are you hungry? Have just this. There's nothing else.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 만 is the SPOTLIGHT — the context confirms there's nothing else ('다른 건 없어요'), so 만 is correct. 도 would imply there are other options too, which contradicts the sentence.

inlineExercises.prompt: 카드___ 결제할게요. (I will pay by card.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 카드로 means by card or using a card as the method. 도 means also and 만 means only, so neither marks the payment method.
도 adds “too/also” to 물. 주세요 makes it a polite ordering request.
주다 becomes 주세요 when you politely ask someone to give something. 도 on 영수증 means “receipt too.”

bullets: 도 = SHOPPING CART: adds one more item or person to what already exists. Replaces 은/는, 이/가, 을/를 — never stacks on top of them.
만 = SPOTLIGHT: limits the sentence to exactly one thing, excluding everything else. Place it directly after the word you want to isolate.
로/으로 = CHANNEL SELECTOR: marks the method, means, or tool of an action. Use 로 after vowels or ㄹ; use 으로 after other consonants.

writingTask.prompt: Order at a café counter: ask for one item, add one more thing, and say how you'll pay.
writingTask.hint: Use N도 for 'also' and N만 for 'only', and (으)로 for the payment method (카드로); end a request with 주세요.
writingTask.model: 커피 한 잔만 주세요. 물도 주세요. 카드로 계산할게요.
writingTask.modelEn: Just one coffee, please. Water too, please. I'll pay by card.

canDo: Add one more thing with N도 and limit to one with N만
Say the payment method or means with N(으)로 (카드로, 현금으로)
Make a simple request with 주세요 (커피 하나 주세요)
Ask the price and respond (얼마예요? · 됩니다/돼요)
